name: Learning::NSW Year 9::Pythagoras::Principles
description: 28 cards on right triangles, choosing legs and hypotenuse, square areas, rearranging, common Pythagorean triples, scaling, units and exact lengths. Every answer has an explanatory diagram. Year 9 practice and foundation review; not a complete course.

cards.front: State Pythagoras’ theorem for a right triangle with legs a and b and hypotenuse c.
cards.back: a² + b² = c². The hypotenuse c is opposite the right angle.

cards.front: How do you identify the hypotenuse, even when a right triangle is drawn upside down?
cards.back: Find the right angle; the side opposite it is the hypotenuse and the longest side.

cards.front: In a² + b² = c², why can a and b swap names but c cannot swap with a leg?
cards.back: Addition lets the legs swap; c must remain the hypotenuse opposite the right angle.

cards.front: A sketch looks right-angled but has no angle marking or measurements. Why is that insufficient for Pythagoras?
cards.back: A sketch is not proof. You need a stated, marked or established right angle.

cards.front: Triangle ABC is right-angled at A. Which side must be the hypotenuse?
cards.back: BC, because it is opposite the right angle at A.

cards.front: What does a² + b² = c² mean if you draw a square on each side of a right triangle?
cards.back: The areas of the two squares on the legs add to the area of the square on the hypotenuse.

cards.front: What formula finds a missing hypotenuse from known legs a and b?
cards.back: c = √(a² + b²): square, add, then take the square root.

cards.front: What formula finds missing leg b from hypotenuse c and other leg a?
cards.back: b = √(c² − a²): square, subtract, then take the square root.

cards.front: A right triangle has hypotenuse 17 cm and a leg 15 cm. Why subtract 15² from 17²?
cards.back: The hypotenuse square equals both leg squares combined; subtracting one leaves the other.

cards.front: You find x² = 81 when calculating a triangle’s side. What is x?
cards.back: 9, because √81 = 9 and a side length is positive.

cards.front: A right triangle’s legs are 300 cm and 4 m. Find its hypotenuse in metres.
cards.back: 5 m. First convert 300 cm to 3 m; then √(3² + 4²) = 5.

cards.front: If c² = 25 cm², what is the hypotenuse length and its unit?
cards.back: c = 5 cm. Taking the square root converts squared centimetres back to centimetres.

cards.front: What is a Pythagorean triple?
cards.back: Three positive integers whose two smaller squares sum to the largest square.

cards.front: A right triangle has legs 3 and 4. Complete the common triple by giving its hypotenuse.
A right triangle has legs 5 and 12. Complete the common triple by giving its hypotenuse.
A right triangle has legs 8 and 15. Complete the common triple by giving its hypotenuse.
A right triangle has legs 7 and 24. Complete the common triple by giving its hypotenuse.
A right triangle has legs 9 and 40. Complete the common triple by giving its hypotenuse.
A right triangle has legs 6 cm and 8 cm. Use the 3–4–5 pattern to find its hypotenuse.
cards.back: 10 cm: multiply every side of 3–4–5 by 2.

cards.front: A right triangle has legs 9 cm and 12 cm. Use the 3–4–5 pattern to find its hypotenuse.
cards.back: 15 cm: multiply every side of 3–4–5 by 3.

cards.front: A right triangle has legs 12 cm and 16 cm. Use the 3–4–5 pattern to find its hypotenuse.
cards.back: 20 cm: multiply every side of 3–4–5 by 4.

cards.front: A right triangle has legs 0.6 m and 0.8 m. Use a familiar side ratio to find its hypotenuse.
cards.back: 1 m: these are 3–4–5 lengths multiplied by 0.2.

cards.front: Why does multiplying every side of a Pythagorean triple by the same positive number preserve the right angle?
cards.back: Each square gains the same factor k², so a² + b² = c² remains true.

cards.front: How can side lengths 9, 12 and 15 establish that a triangle is right-angled?
cards.back: 9² + 12² = 15²; by the converse of Pythagoras, the angle opposite 15 is 90°.

cards.front: Why are 4, 5 and 6 not a Pythagorean triple?
cards.back: 4² + 5² = 41, but 6² = 36. The squares do not match.

cards.front: A right triangle has legs 5 cm and 5 cm. Give its hypotenuse exactly, without a decimal approximation.
A right isosceles triangle has equal legs x. What is its hypotenuse in terms of x?
cards.back: x√2, because c² = x² + x² = 2x².

cards.front: A right triangle has legs 8 cm and 11 cm. Find the hypotenuse to one decimal place.
cards.back: 13.6 cm: keep √185 unrounded until the final answer.
